When context distinguishes a specific political entity from a broader country label, give the specific entity (for example, “People’s Republic of China,” not merely “China”). For people, give the full name rather than only a surname; include an honorific when the clue explicitly signals it, such as “knighted” requiring “Sir,” but do not add unsupported titles. For vocabulary clues, match the requested part of speech and inflection: if the clue asks for a term meaning the act or manner of following a winding course, use the corresponding form “meandering,” not the base verb “meander.”
